relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.evidence: graduated 1842 from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute as civil engineer.

relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.evidence: Studies at Harvard, published translations from German, but could not conclude his studies, because in 1846 he was sent to Calcutta

relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.evidence: After three years he came to Benares, where in 1850 “he was appointed in the Government College to a post, which was converted in 1853 into an Anglo-Sanskrit professorship. In 1855 he was transferred

relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.evidence: worked 1864-69 as Librarian of India Office.

relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.role: (unpaid) Professor of Sanskrit, Hindustani and Indian Jurisprudence
relations.evidence: In 1864–69 also (unpaid) Professor of Sanskrit, Hindustani and Indian Jurisprudence at King’s College in London.

relations.subject: Fitzedward Hall
relations.evidence: In 1869 resigned, apparently because of false accusations (he was accused by Goldstücker, also otherwise known as quarrelsome, of being a drunkard and a foreign spy)
